source_text: Praescribit autem veritas primo malum id est peccatum dici non posse, quod ita est, ut eius natura compulerit, peccatumque nihil esse aliud quam exorbitantem a calle iustitiae liberam voluntatem.
pass_a_gloss: But truth first prescribes that that cannot be called evil, that is sin, which is so as its nature has compelled, and that sin is nothing other than a free will going out of the path of justice.

lemmas.lexica: LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will

pass_b_english: Truth, however, first lays down that what is as its nature compelled it to be cannot be called evil—that is, sin—and that sin is nothing other than a free will straying from the path of justice.

choices.why: Freedom to abstain is required for will and sin.
Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
